title: Potato Pathology, Immunity & Storage Biology — Defense, Stress, Wounds and Postharvest Life
purpose: Treat the potato as a living host and postharvest organ: immune recognition, pathogens, abiotic stress, wound repair, respiration, dormancy, sugar remodeling and clonal disease carryover.

immune_architecture.surface_recognition: Cell-surface pattern-recognition receptors detect pathogen-associated or damage-associated cues and initiate defense signalling.
immune_architecture.intracellular_recognition: NLR immune receptors can recognize pathogen effectors and activate strong defense responses.
immune_architecture.late_blight: Phytophthora infestans is an oomycete pathogen; many Rpi resistance genes have been discovered in wild Solanum relatives and used in breeding.
immune_architecture.durability: Single resistance genes can be defeated by pathogen evolution; pyramiding/stacking receptors and quantitative resistance can broaden or prolong resistance but does not guarantee permanence.
immune_architecture.defense_cost: Defense, growth and reproduction share resources and regulatory networks, so resistance is part of a trade-off system.

examples: Ralstonia solanacearum bacterial wilt in susceptible regions

abiotic_stress_network.systems_rule: Combined stresses can produce responses not predictable by simply adding single-stress responses.

postharvest_life.respiration: Harvested tubers remain metabolically active and respire.
postharvest_life.lenticels: Major routes for tuber gas exchange; morphology and distribution can change during storage and dormancy break.
postharvest_life.water_loss: Periderm limits dehydration while lenticels and wounds increase exchange pathways.
postharvest_life.wound_response: Suberized closing layers and wound periderm reduce water loss and pathogen ingress after injury.
postharvest_life.dormancy: A regulated physiological interval that progresses toward sprouting depending on genotype, age and storage environment.
postharvest_life.cold_induced_sweetening: Low-temperature storage can shift starch/sucrose metabolism toward reducing sugars, with vacuolar invertase a major control point.
postharvest_life.food_quality: Reducing sugars influence fry color and acrylamide formation during high-temperature processing.

clonal_health.seed_degeneration: Vegetative propagation can carry viruses and other pathogens from one planting generation to the next.
clonal_health.clean_seed: Meristem culture, indexing/testing, sanitation and certified seed systems are used to reduce pathogen load.
clonal_health.rule: Clonal fidelity preserves both useful genotype and biological burdens unless health management interrupts transmission.

glycoalkaloids.regulation: GAME-family enzymes and associated transcriptional/regulatory networks control biosynthesis from cholesterol-derived precursors.
glycoalkaloids.food_boundary: Greening and glycoalkaloid accumulation are related stress/light responses but chlorophyll itself is not the toxin; excessive glycoalkaloids are the food-safety concern.

multiomics_and_testing.2025_stress_work: Potato studies now combine deep phenotyping and multi-omics to resolve responses to single and combined heat, drought and flooding stresses.
multiomics_and_testing.evidence_rule: Separate resistance-gene presence from actual resistance phenotype, which depends on allele function, expression, pathogen genotype, environment and genetic background.
